compute.title: Compute Engine
compute.summary: Vyomi's own Compute Engine v1 API core keeps instances, disks, snapshots, templates and groups as records, and attaches a real Docker container (offline) or an in-browser v86 Linux VM (Nano) to a running instance.
wire: SSH via ssh-keys metadata (offline container, or vyomi-tunnel to the Nano VM)

offline.notes: The core (core/gcp_compute_core.py, gcp_compute_instances_core.py) holds the resource model; a running instance is a real Docker container with sshd (LXD and Multipass are also recognised by the live-backend list). Disks and snapshots are metadata only.

nano.notes: The same core holds the records. With in-browser VMs turned on, an instance is a real 32-bit x86 Alpine VM (v86) in the tab, not the boot image you picked; with them off the instance stays a record with no guest.

differs: Instances are READY immediately and operations complete inline; there is no provisioning delay.
Disks, snapshots, instant snapshots and machine images hold no block data; a restored disk is an empty disk of the same size.

Serial port output is Vyomi's own lifecycle log, not a guest kernel's console text; instances.getScreenshot stays FAILED_PRECONDITION (no framebuffer), the console renders the serial tail as an image instead.

Offline has no guest agent: getGuestAttributes returns FAILED_PRECONDITION; OS info is read from the running container. On Nano the guest is a 32-bit Alpine VM, RAM is its disk (Terminate discards it), a background tab runs it several times slower.
Nano VMs have no general internet egress (only plain-HTTP URLs that allow CORS), so git clone, apt and pip from the internet do not work there.
Snapshot and instance schedules are evaluated lazily on Compute API calls, with missed fires caught up; time zones fall back to UTC when the runtime has no tz database.
Instance group autoscaling policies are not simulated; resize is manual or via a rolling update.
OS Login (IAM-based key distribution) is not enforced; reservations and committed-use discounts are accounting records and nothing is billed.
notInScope: Google's physical hosts, hypervisor, live migration and host maintenance events
Real GPUs, TPUs and Bare Metal Solution hardware
Real block storage, replication RPO measurement and cross-zone disk replication
Billing, quotas as Google enforces them, and Google's usage-based Recommender AI

service-health.title: Google Cloud incidents (Service Health feed)
service-health.summary: A Vyomi-owned Service Health API that reports the health of your simulated project only.

offline.notes: core/gcp_servicehealth_core.py keeps per-service status and an incident list in the Compute store; no external source.

nano.notes: Same core in the browser.

differs: Not Google's real status feed: every simulated service is Available and the incident history is empty until you inject a test incident.
Injecting, updating, resolving and deleting incidents are Vyomi extensions; every event is marked vyomiSimulated.
notInScope: Real Google Cloud outage data
Impact assessment of Google's own infrastructure

rollouts.title: Rollouts (rolling template rollout)
rollouts.summary: A rollout rolls an instance template over managed instance groups wave by wave through Vyomi's MIG engine.
wire: Vyomi extension on the Compute API (rollout create takes instanceTemplate; plans carry vyomiManagedInstanceGroups)

offline.notes: New members are created and old ones deleted (PROACTIVE rolling replace), each wave is checked for RUNNING members, and the group rolls back on failure or :rollback. Members are Docker-backed containers where the compute runtime is on.

nano.notes: Same engine over Nano's records; members are records unless in-browser VMs are on (not verified for rollouts).

differs: Waves advance on request (:advance); there is no time-based or metric-based validation.
No organization- or folder-scoped plans; Google-managed product updates are not rolled out.
notInScope: Google-managed fleet updates
Metric-based validation of waves

vm-manager.title: VM Manager (OS Config)
vm-manager.summary: OS Config patch jobs and deployments are a real control plane; offline they run the package manager inside the instance container.

offline.notes: Patch jobs on a running VM with metadata enable-osconfig=TRUE run apt-get, yum, dnf or apk via docker exec and report the exit status.

nano.notes: Control plane only; no package manager runs.

differs: A running VM without enable-osconfig=TRUE is NO_AGENT_DETECTED; OS policy assignments are recorded and report SUCCEEDED but are never enforced.
No guest agent exists, so nothing is applied on Nano.
notInScope: Google's OS Config guest agent
Real OS inventory beyond what the container reports

bare-metal-and-tpu.title: Bare Metal Solution and Cloud TPU
bare-metal-and-tpu.summary: Bare Metal Solution is not simulated; Cloud TPU v2 is a record-level API with a state machine.
wire: tpu.googleapis.com v2 nodes (create, get, list, patch, delete, start, stop)

offline.notes: TPU nodes move CREATING to READY as records; Bare Metal Solution has no implementation.

nano.notes: Same TPU records; Bare Metal Solution unavailable.

differs: Bare Metal Solution is marked not_simulated; use Compute Engine instances for local servers.
TPU nodes run no workload.
notInScope: Physical bare metal servers
TPU hardware

storage.title: Cloud Storage
storage.summary: Vyomi's own GCS JSON API v1 core holds buckets and objects in the appliance state and, on the appliance, also writes object bytes through to a fake-gcs-server container.

offline.notes: core/gcp_storage_core.py is the engine and its metadata and inline bytes persist in the appliance state; bytes are additionally mirrored to fake-gcs-server when CLOUDLEARN_GCS_URL is reachable, and skipped (logged once) when it is not.

tech: in-memory object store snapshotted to IndexedDB
nano.notes: The same core holds buckets and objects in browser memory with IndexedDB snapshots; no fake-gcs-server and no external storage.

differs: Bucket create, patch and delete complete synchronously; real cross-location moves can return a long-running operation.
Lifecycle, soft-delete and Autoclass sweeps run lazily on the next request, not on Google's schedule; AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload never fires.
Public access prevention and bucket IAM are enforced on write (setIamPolicy), but the static-website host ignores IAM and public access prevention.

Batch operations and Storage Insights are Vyomi sub-resources of /storage/v1 (batchOperations, insightsDatasets), not the separate storagebatchoperations / storageinsights services; a batch job finishes synchronously.
Insights datasets export into a BigQuery stand-in that runs SQLite SQL, not GoogleSQL.
HMAC keys are issued and listed but HMAC-signed requests are never verified; CSEK data is encrypted with a SHA-256 counter-mode keystream, not AES.
Anywhere Cache, Turbo replication and requester-pays keep one copy and meter no billing: there is no cache tier, replication guarantee or charge.
Only request count is metered into Cloud Monitoring; no error-rate, bandwidth or latency series.
Versioned and soft-deleted generations live in an in-process archive, not a separately durable record.
notInScope: Google's multi-region storage, durability and replication
Storage class pricing, egress billing and retrieval fees
Real KMS-backed encryption of bytes at rest beyond what the registry lists
Google's Security Command Center bucket detectors

object-enrichments.title: Object enrichments
object-enrichments.summary: Rules run local extractors over each newly uploaded object and write the results into its custom metadata.
wire: results visible as vyomi-enrich-* object metadata

tech: tesseract (optional, if installed on the host)
offline.notes: Extractors: size, SHA-256, magic-byte type, text/JSON/CSV facts, image dimensions, PDF page count and title; OCR only when tesseract exists on the host.

nano.notes: Same extractors in the browser; no OCR.

differs: Not Document AI: no classification, entity or form extraction.
Runs synchronously on upload and reads at most the first 8 MiB; existing objects are only processed when a rule's :run is called.
notInScope: Document AI and Vertex AI based extraction

insights.title: Storage Insights and inventory reports
insights.summary: Insights dataset configs snapshot buckets and objects into a SQLite-backed BigQuery stand-in; inventory report configs write real CSV reports.

offline.notes: core/gcp_storageinsights_core.py and the BigQuery stand-in (core/gcp_bigquery_core.py) run on SQLite.

nano.notes: Same code in the browser.

differs: SQL is SQLite's dialect, not GoogleSQL (no STRUCT/ARRAY/UNNEST, SAFE_ functions, QUALIFY); only SELECT is accepted.
Report generation is lazy (on read), not on Google's 24-48 h schedule; :runNow is a Vyomi addition.
notInScope: Real BigQuery slots, billing and storage

firestore.title: Firestore
firestore.summary: Vyomi's own Firestore REST v1 and Admin v1 core stores documents, indexes, rules, TTL, backups and PITR in the appliance state; the Google Firestore emulator container is not the data plane in v4.
wire: Firestore Admin v1 (databases, indexes, fields, backups, import/export)

offline.notes: core/gcp_firestore_core.py is served through the unified ingress over the appliance state. The compose file still starts the Google Firestore emulator, but v4 uses it only to adopt documents held by pre-v4 setups (core/appliance_stores.py); whether a gRPC client against that emulator shares v4 state is not verified.

nano.notes: The same core holds documents in browser memory with IndexedDB snapshots. gRPC clients cannot reach it; REST transport only.

differs: Database create, update and delete complete synchronously; the real API returns a long-running operation.
Composite indexes report READY immediately; the BUILDING phase is not modelled, and the index coverage check matches exact field path plus order only, not full multi-field prefix matching.
Vector search (findNearest) is an exact brute-force scan, not approximate nearest neighbour.
Security rules are enforced for client-SDK style requests but Firebase ID token signatures are not verified (same as the Firebase emulator).
TTL expiry is checked lazily on next access; backup schedules take one backup on creation and do not fire later ticks.
Export and import use a Vyomi-internal JSON snapshot in the simulator's Cloud Storage, not the protobuf/LevelDB layout, so it is not portable to real Firestore.
Point-in-time recovery supports reads at a past readTime but has no whole-database PITR restore.
Insights, Usage and Key Visualizer show current-session telemetry only, with no history; Key Visualizer buckets are a hash, not tablet ranges.
Datastore mode lacks transaction read isolation, GQL beyond simple SELECT, multi-kind queries and export/import.
notInScope: Google's distributed storage, multi-region replication and SLA
Billing and quotas
Historical usage charts built from Cloud Monitoring

datastore.title: Datastore mode
datastore.summary: Datastore API entities and indexes served by Vyomi's own Datastore core.
wire: Datastore API v1 (lookup, runQuery, commit, beginTransaction)

offline.notes: core/gcp_datastore_core.py.

nano.notes: Same core in the browser.

differs: Transactions are all-or-nothing on commit but reads inside a transaction are not snapshotted.
GQL supports SELECT ... FROM ... WHERE ... ORDER BY ... LIMIT/OFFSET only.
notInScope: Datastore export/import
Multi-kind queries

pubsub.title: Pub/Sub
pubsub.summary: Vyomi's own Pub/Sub REST v1 core implements topics, subscriptions, snapshots and schemas on the same messaging store as SNS/SQS; the Google Pub/Sub emulator container is not the v4 data plane.
wire: Pub/Sub REST API v1 /v1/projects/{p}/topics, subscriptions, snapshots, schemas

offline.notes: core/gcp_pubsub_core.py is served through the unified ingress over AppStatePubsubStore. The compose file still starts the Google Pub/Sub emulator, used in v4 only to adopt topics and subscriptions from pre-v4 setups; gRPC client access to state is not verified.

nano.notes: The same core in browser memory with IndexedDB snapshots; REST only, no gRPC.

differs: Ack-deadline redelivery and retry backoff take effect on the next pull, not by background timer.
Push subscriptions store the endpoint but Vyomi never calls it; use pull to receive messages.
enableExactlyOnceDelivery is stored but redelivered messages are not deduplicated.
CMEK kmsKeyName is stored but no Cloud KMS encryption happens; BINARY Avro and Protocol Buffer schema encodings are not validated.
Subscription filters support a documented subset of the language; the ':' substring form and CEL expressions are rejected or unsupported.
Write to BigQuery delivery is not modelled; Write to Cloud Storage delivers real newline-delimited objects into the simulator's GCS.
Topic ingestion works from Cloud Storage only; Kinesis, Event Hubs, Confluent and CDC sources are rejected at create.
Message transforms run a documented subset of JavaScript (no loops, classes, async, regex).
Metrics are gauge snapshots of running totals mirrored into Cloud Monitoring, not Google's per-minute deltas.
notInScope: Google's global message routing, ordering guarantees across regions and throughput limits
Real push delivery to external HTTPS endpoints
Billing and quotas

secret-manager.title: Secret Manager
secret-manager.summary: Vyomi's own Secret Manager REST v1 core stores secrets and versions in a key-value store in the appliance state.
wire: Secret Manager REST API v1 /v1/projects/{p}/secrets and regional locations/{l}/secrets

offline.notes: core/gcp_secretmanager_core.py through the unified ingress over the appliance state store (core/appliance_stores.py). The compose Vault container is only read to adopt pre-v4 secrets; it is not the store.

nano.notes: Same core with the key-value store in browser memory and IndexedDB snapshots.

differs: Rotation settings are validated and stored but rotation is not run, and no SECRET_ROTATE notification is published.
CMEK and replication locations are validated; data is not encrypted with the named key.
Per-secret IAM is enforced for the listed operations, with a curated role set.
Version lifecycle events publish real Pub/Sub messages and Cloud Logging entries; read/access calls and the full Cloud Audit Log protoPayload shape are not recorded.
notInScope: Google's replication and KMS-backed encryption at rest
Billing, quotas and access-transparency logs
sources: core/appliance_stores.py (header: Secret Manager slot, Vault adoption)

kms.title: Cloud KMS
kms.summary: Vyomi's own Cloud KMS REST v1 core keeps key rings, keys and versions and does the cryptography with Python standard-library code, not an HSM or Vault.

offline.notes: core/gcp_kms_core.py with the shared KeyStore/KmsEngine (core/kms_keystore.py): deterministic authenticated envelope encryption in stdlib. Vault is only read to decrypt pre-v4 ciphertext.

nano.notes: Same engine in the browser; key material is in browser memory and IndexedDB snapshots.

differs: Software protection only: HSM, External and External-via-VPC protection levels are not simulated.
Key import supports symmetric 256-bit software keys only (RSA-3072/4096 wrapping with AES-KWP).
Rotation period is stored but never runs on its own; use Rotate key.
Autokey is project-level only (no folder/organization hierarchy) and other Vyomi services do not call CreateKeyHandle automatically.
Ciphertext is Vyomi's own envelope format, not interchangeable with real Cloud KMS ciphertext.
notInScope: FIPS 140-2 hardware security modules
External key managers (EKM)
Google-managed key rotation and key access justifications

sql.title: Cloud SQL
sql.summary: Vyomi's own Cloud SQL Admin core keeps instance metadata and, on the appliance, backs each instance with a real database on a shared Postgres or MySQL container.
wire: Postgres and MySQL wire protocols to the host:port shown in the console (offline)

offline.notes: core/gcp_cloudsql_core.py holds the control plane; core/gcp_sql_engine.py creates one database and login role per instance on the shared engine so unmodified drivers can connect. If the engine is unreachable the instance degrades to metadata only.

nano.notes: The control plane is the same core; SQL in Cloud SQL Studio runs on sqlite3 per the registry, and the core references PGlite as the browser Postgres engine. Which engine serves a given instance is not verified. No raw Postgres/MySQL TCP wire in the browser.

differs: Instances are RUNNABLE immediately and every operation completes synchronously with status DONE.
Stop and start toggle settings.activationPolicy; no compute is torn down. CPU and memory utilisation are not measured.
IAM database authentication is stored but never checked on connect; only the password gates access.

Backups snapshot control-plane metadata and row data for restore/clone; they are not written to Cloud Storage. Registry entries disagree on whether automated daily backups are scheduled (one says they run from the scheduler tick, another says not scheduled): not verified.
Read replicas mirror databases and users synchronously but can still be written to directly.
SSL mode ENCRYPTED_ONLY is enforced only on Cloud SQL Studio's query path; client-certificate validation is not performed.
CMEK key existence and region are checked but disk data is not encrypted with the key.
Export and import use the simulator's own Cloud Storage; offline MySQL-backed instances cannot export or import, and BAK/SQL Server files are not simulated.
notInScope: SQL Server and AlloyDB engines (not verified as implemented)
Google's HA failover, maintenance and managed storage
Query Insights ML analysis, billing and quotas

memorystore.title: Memorystore for Redis
memorystore.summary: Vyomi's own Memorystore control plane (instances, failover, upgrade, AUTH) is backed offline by one shared Valkey container and has no data plane on Nano.
wire: Memorystore for Redis REST API v1 /v1/projects/{p}/locations/{l}/instances
Redis protocol to the shown endpoint (offline)

offline.notes: core/gcp_redis_core.py is the control plane; instances share the single Valkey container, which serves the Redis protocol at the endpoint when configured.

nano.notes: Control plane only: the instance host is a deterministic address and there is no Redis data plane in the browser.

differs: Instances are READY immediately; failover swaps zones instantly with no replication lag.
Import and export validate the gs:// path and complete, but no RDB file is read or written.
Read replicas are a replica count and read endpoint on the same instance; no separate replica processes run.
serverCaCerts are placeholders; a client cannot negotiate TLS against them.
Maintenance windows are recorded and never executed.
Memory, clients and command metrics come from the shared Valkey INFO, shared across instances.
notInScope: Redis Cluster / Memorystore for Redis Cluster and Valkey service variants (not verified)
Real replication, persistence and SLA
Billing

run.title: Cloud Run
run.summary: Vyomi's own Cloud Run Admin v2 core models services, revisions, jobs, worker pools and domain mappings; source builds use BuildKit offline and a daemonless layer builder on Nano.
wire: Cloud Run Admin API v2 /v2/projects/{p}/locations/{l}/services, jobs, workerPools

offline.notes: core/gcp_run_core.py holds the control plane in the space's gcp_run state slot. Source deploys build the Dockerfile on BuildKit and push the image into the simulated Artifact Registry. Whether containers are executed offline is not verified (the registry says they are not).

nano.notes: The same core; the layer builder produces a real OCI image (gzip tar layers, sha256 digests) with no container runtime. A GitHub source build fails because Nano has no outbound HTTP.

differs: Billing is not metered; cpuIdle is mirrored only.

Vyomi does not build or run arbitrary container images; the registry states containers are not executed (the core docstring mentions the Pro Docker backend, not verified end to end). Deliveries to container-image services are recorded only.
Probes, volumes, ephemeral disks, Cloud SQL sockets and CMEK are validated and stored but nothing is mounted, started or encrypted.
HTTP/2, session affinity and VPC egress are validated configuration only; the request path is plain HTTP/1.1 with no load balancer.
Custom-domain mappings return illustrative DNS records and no TLS certificate; revision-tag URLs are served by Vyomi's own endpoint.
Long-running operations complete inline (done=true).

GPU (Dev Simplified): only nvidia-l4 is accepted; the config is validated and stored, the revision is annotated vyomi.dev/gpu-status, but no GPU is passed through to revisions even if the host Docker has an NVIDIA runtime. Nano never has a GPU.
Continuous deploy and source deploy work against Vyomi's built-in git host (Gitea) with a Dockerfile; GitHub, Cloud Source Repositories, buildpacks and Cloud Build worker pools are not simulated.
notInScope: Google's autoscaled container fleet, cold starts and request routing
Real traffic metrics, latency and instance counts
GPU hardware, billing and quotas

binary-authorization.title: Binary Authorization
binary-authorization.summary: Deploy-time image admission against a project policy with ECDSA attestors, evaluated in Vyomi's own core.

offline.notes: core/gcp_binauthz_core.py.

nano.notes: Same core.

differs: Only ECDSA_P256_SHA256 PKIX keys; RSA, other curves and Cloud KMS-backed attestor keys are refused.
GKE/Anthos cluster rules and continuous validation are stored, not enforced.
notInScope: Google-managed attestation services

functions.title: Cloud Run functions
functions.summary: A function is a Cloud Run service in Vyomi's Run core; Python sources are really executed on invoke in Vyomi's sandbox, other runtimes are stored only.
wire: Cloud Functions REST v2 and v1 (cloudfunctions.googleapis.com)
Cloud Run Admin API v2 for the same services

offline.notes: core/gcp_functions_core.py creates the function in the Run store; source zips go to the simulator's GCS and the module text is stored so :call, the HTTPS URL and Eventarc deliveries execute it. Whether the offline sandbox is in-process or a subprocess (core/gcp_function_runtime.py exists) is not verified.

nano.notes: Same core and sandbox in Pyodide; webhook tools and anything needing egress cannot run in the browser.

differs: Python sources run; the registry says other runtimes are stored and validated only, while the core docstring also names JavaScript: JavaScript execution is not verified.
Container-deployed services are metered but not executed; latency for them is near zero.
Metrics and logs are fed by real invokes and trigger deliveries only; instance count is derived from min instances and recent activity, not a scheduler.
Event triggers: Pub/Sub sourced triggers deliver for real; Storage and Audit Log providers follow the Eventarc rules; unsupported providers are rejected at create.
YAML view is read-only; HTTP/2, session affinity and VPC egress are configuration only.
GPU (Dev Simplified): nvidia-l4 config validated and stored, CPU-only in practice; Nano never has a GPU.
notInScope: Google's build service, runtime images and autoscaling fleet
Real GPU acceleration
Billing

kubernetes.title: Google Kubernetes Engine
kubernetes.summary: Vyomi's own GKE v1 core models clusters and node pools and keeps a simulated Kubernetes object store behind each cluster; real k3s containers are used only when the offline appliance is started with the k3s backend.
wire: Kubernetes REST under .../clusters/{c}/k8s/... (simulated store or the k3s API server)
GKE Hub, gkebackup and Config Management APIs

offline.notes: Default: control plane plus the simulated object store in core/gcp_gke_dataplane_core.py. With VYOMI_K8S_BACKEND=k3s and a reachable Docker daemon a cluster gets a real k3s API server and the /k8s path goes to it; the core docstring ties this to the Max tier.

nano.notes: Control plane and simulated object store only; no Kubernetes API server runs in the browser.

differs: Without k3s, kubectl against the displayed endpoint cannot connect (no listener at that address); objects are reachable through the cluster's /k8s path in Vyomi.
Simulated workloads do not schedule or run containers; workload health comes from stored objects.
PersistentVolumeClaims bind to auto-provisioned PVs with real default StorageClasses, but no disk exists.
Backup for GKE snapshots control-plane config and objects, not volumes.
Policy Controller admission (K8sRequiredLabels) is enforced against the simulated store.
Operations complete inline; the logs section shows control-plane operations, not container logs.
Observability numbers are derived from stored objects, not node metrics.
notInScope: Google-managed control plane, node auto-upgrade and node VMs
Real cluster networking, load balancers and Workload Identity
Fleet-wide features beyond registration records

networking.title: VPC network
networking.summary: Vyomi's own Compute networking core models VPCs, subnets, firewall rules, routes and addresses and answers reachability from a shared network evaluator; offline it can also enforce rules on real Docker bridges with nftables.
wire: Compute Engine REST /compute/v1 (networks, subnetworks, firewalls, routes, addresses, routers)
Service Networking and Serverless VPC Access APIs

offline.notes: Rules are evaluated logically by default. With VYOMI_NETSIM_ENFORCE=1 or auto and the Docker compute backend, one bridge per subnet and an nftables table per space enforce them on real packets (core/netsim/enforce.py).

nano.notes: Only the logical evaluator; no packets exist, so flow logs and Connectivity Tests come from analysis, not traffic.

differs: Firewall hit counts and Firewall Insights are not computed.
Network firewall policies are regional only (no organization/folder hierarchy).
Peering, Shared VPC, private service connection and Serverless VPC Access are real stateful resources with their constraints, but forward no traffic.
Cloud Interconnect, VPN and BYOIP are control-plane records: ACTIVE means enabled, not carrying traffic; BYOIP prefixes validate immediately and nothing is advertised.
Packet mirroring and VPC Flow Logs produce data only when netsim enforcement is on (offline); Nano flow records come from the logical evaluator.
Cloud NAT gives VMs egress in tests and, with enforcement, offline traffic; no real NAT gateway exists.
notInScope: Google's global backbone, load balancing and DDoS protection
Physical interconnect circuits and BGP sessions
Firewall Insights and Network Analyzer ML

logs.title: Cloud Logging
logs.summary: Vyomi's own Cloud Logging v2 core stores entries, sinks, log-based metrics, buckets and views and evaluates the Logging filter language.
wire: Cloud Logging REST API v2 (entries:write, entries:list, sinks, metrics, buckets, views)

offline.notes: core/gcp_logging_core.py with the persisted space store (routes/gcp_logging.py). Admin Activity audit entries are produced by core/gcp_audit_core.py.

nano.notes: Same core in browser memory with IndexedDB snapshots.

differs: Observability Analytics SQL is a BigQuery SQL subset (SELECT/WHERE/ORDER BY/LIMIT over one bucket), no joins or subqueries.
Metric usage and router volume are live counts of stored entries, not billed bytes or historical exports.
The _Default and _Required buckets are seeded and not deletable, as in Google.
Correlate by trace groups up to 20 traces; span trees are not built here.
Only the services listed in gcp_audit_core produce Admin Activity entries; Data Access logs are generated only for the IAM Admin Read toggles the IAM core enforces.
notInScope: Google's log ingestion pipeline, retention and cross-region storage
Billing for log volume
Log Analytics linked BigQuery datasets (real BigQuery)

monitoring.title: Cloud Monitoring
monitoring.summary: Vyomi's own Cloud Monitoring v3 core stores alert policies, uptime checks, dashboards, groups, SLOs and time series from simulator activity; offline it can also mirror samples into VictoriaMetrics.
wire: Cloud Monitoring REST API v3 (alertPolicies, notificationChannels, timeSeries, metricDescriptors, uptimeCheckConfigs, services/SLOs, groups, snoozes)

offline.notes: core/gcp_monitoring_core.py evaluates alert conditions against stored series. When CLOUDLEARN_VICTORIAMETRICS_URL is set each sample is also mirrored to VictoriaMetrics (providers/gcp_monitoring_console.py); the core does not depend on it.

nano.notes: Same core in the browser; series come only from activity inside the tab.

differs: Notification channels are created and verified but no email, SMS, Slack or webhook is ever sent.

Uptime checks are probed by Vyomi (run_uptime_probes), but with no outbound network a check on an arbitrary external host fails closed; Compute-instance checks follow the instance's RUNNING state; results do not vary by region. The registry's uptime config entry says no probe is dispatched; the probing entry is the newer text.
Metrics Explorer runs Builder queries; PromQL mode is not parsed.
Metrics management byte/sample volume and read counts, Cost Explorer BigQuery export and Error Reporting grouping are not Google's; Error Reporting shows what Vyomi derives from ERROR log entries.
No Ops Agent runs in simulated VMs; the heartbeat is derived from instance metadata, and host metrics arrive only when a runtime pushes them.
Trace Explorer stores and queries spans written through the Trace API; no APM, Profiler or automatic instrumentation exists.
Application monitoring links App Hub applications to discovered resources only; alert policies attach by label.
notInScope: Google's metrics pipeline, retention and aggregation scale
Managed Service for Prometheus
Real agent telemetry, Profiler and golden-signal dashboards

iam-admin.title: IAM & Admin
iam-admin.summary: Vyomi's own IAM, Resource Manager, Org Policy, PAM and federation cores keep policies, service accounts, roles and pools in the appliance state and enforce a defined subset of them.
wire: IAM API (serviceAccounts, keys, roles, workloadIdentityPools, workforcePools)
Org Policy v2, Policy Troubleshooter, PAM, Cloud Identity Groups

offline.notes: core/gcp_iam_core.py, gcp_iam_policy.py, gcp_iamcredentials_core.py, gcp_pam_core.py, gcp_wif_core.py and gcp_resourcemanager_core.py, over AppStateGcpIamStore (core/appliance_stores.py).

nano.notes: The same cores in browser memory with IndexedDB snapshots.

differs: Service account keys are real stateful resources but the private key is synthetic and authenticates nothing outside Vyomi.
Policies are enforced inside Vyomi for the services that consult them (Secret Manager, KMS, Artifact Registry, buckets, etc.), using a curated set of predefined roles.
Only two predefined org policy constraints are enforced for real (service account creation and key creation), plus a simulation of four constraints against existing resources.
Recommender is not run: the history shows only changes applied in Vyomi.

Workload and workforce federation: pool and provider resources are stateful and the STS exchange evaluates attribute mapping and a CEL subset; real external IdPs are not contacted and workforce browser sign-in is not simulated.
Policy Analyzer and Asset Inventory index only what Vyomi models, without inherited organization/folder policy; Security Insights are a small set of IAM lint rules.
A single backing organization is created per project; Cloud Identity directory sync is not performed.
Access Approval and Access Transparency have no staff to approve; their pages are derived from audit entries.
notInScope: Google's global IAM evaluation and propagation
Google Workspace / Cloud Identity directory
IAM Recommender ML
Real external OIDC/SAML identity providers

pam.title: Privileged Access Manager
pam.summary: Entitlements, grants and approvals with justification enforcement.

offline.notes: core/gcp_pam_core.py (routes/gcp_pam.py).

nano.notes: Same core.

differs: The audit view shows the grant lifecycle Vyomi records, not the full Cloud Audit Logs trail.
Notification channels are stored; require-justification is enforced.
notInScope: Real notification delivery

identity-aware-proxy.summary: Per-resource IAP enablement and IAM, with checkAccess enforced.

artifacts.title: Artifact Registry
artifacts.summary: Vyomi's own Artifact Registry v1 core stores repositories, packages, versions and tags as metadata, with enforced IAM, CMEK checks, cleanup policies and an advisory-snapshot vulnerability scanner.

offline.notes: core/gcp_artifactregistry_core.py (routes/gcp_artifactregistry.py) in the space state. Images are scanned by the bundled engine (core/vuln_scan_core.py); a real Trivy container report replaces it per image digest only when one has been produced (providers/trivy_runner.py). The shared Docker registry container is referenced only through CLOUDLEARN_REGISTRY_HOST; whether AR uses it is not verified.

nano.notes: Same core; scanning uses the bundled snapshot only, no Trivy.

differs: There is no Docker/Maven/npm/pip daemon: packages are created through the push-sample action, not a real docker push.
The AR control plane stores no layer blobs, so Trivy cannot scan an AR image on its own yet.
Remote repositories store their config but do not proxy upstream; virtual repositories aggregate member repositories and reject direct pushes.
Cleanup policies run lazily on the next read or write, not on a periodic schedule.
Vulnerability data is a bundled snapshot of a few dozen well-known CVEs plus an end-of-life table, not a live feed.
IAM covers a curated role set; CMEK key state is checked on create and push, but data is not encrypted by Cloud KMS.
notInScope: Google's container analysis pipeline and live CVE feeds
Real image layer storage and pull-through caching
Billing and egress

cloudbuild.title: Cloud Build
cloudbuild.summary: Vyomi's own Cloud Build v1 core runs docker build steps on a shared BuildKit builder offline, and builds OCI images with a daemonless layer builder on Nano.
wire: Cloud Build REST API v1 /v1/projects/{p}/builds and /triggers

offline.notes: core/gcp_cloudbuild_core.py runs docker build steps on BuildKit and pushes images into the simulated Artifact Registry; sources come from CI repos on the built-in git host, GitHub (with the user's PAT) or the simulator's GCS.

nano.notes: Builds a real OCI image from Dockerfile COPY/ADD/ENV/CMD etc. without a container runtime; RUN-style execution and outbound fetches are not available in the browser.

differs: Triggers support branch-regex push events through the Vyomi push extension; pull_request, Pub/Sub and webhook triggers and approvals are not simulated.
cloudbuild.yaml is read with a built-in YAML subset parser.
Regional trigger paths are not routed (that URL is Eventarc's).
notInScope: Google-hosted private pools and worker machines
Real GitHub App / Cloud Source Repositories connections
Billing for build minutes

clouddeploy.title: Cloud Deploy
clouddeploy.summary: Vyomi's own Cloud Deploy v1 core runs pipelines, targets, releases and rollouts as a state machine that really updates Cloud Run services or the GKE data plane.
wire: Cloud Deploy REST API v1 deliveryPipelines, targets, releases, rollouts

offline.notes: core/gcp_clouddeploy_core.py (state on the Monitoring store). The deploy job updates the Cloud Run service (canary splits traffic) or replaces the Deployment in the GKE cluster's simulated data plane.

nano.notes: Same logic against Nano's Cloud Run and GKE state.

differs: Skaffold is not run: manifests are not rendered from skaffold.yaml and verify jobs do not execute their container (they succeed unless vyomi-verify=fail).
multiTarget, custom/Anthos targets, hooks, customCanaryDeployment, automations and deploy policies are rejected or stored only.

Real Anthos / custom targets

cloudscheduler.title: Cloud Scheduler
cloudscheduler.summary: Vyomi's own Cloud Scheduler v1 core stores jobs and fires them from a background ticker offline, or lazily on any request on Nano.
wire: App Engine cron.yaml modelled as jobs

offline.notes: core/gcp_cloudscheduler_core.py with a 15 s background ticker; HTTP targets are really sent with retries, Pub/Sub targets publish into the Pub/Sub core.

nano.notes: A due job fires the first time a request touches its project; HTTP targets are recorded as attempted but never invoked (no outbound network).

differs: Missed ticks are never replayed; only the next occurrence is computed.
App Engine HTTP targets and cron.yaml jobs are recorded as attempted only; App Engine is not modelled.
OAuth/OIDC settings are returned as configured; the offline appliance sends a placeholder bearer token.

backupdr.title: Backup and DR Service
backupdr.summary: Vyomi's own Backup and DR v1 core protects Compute instances and disks by taking Vyomi snapshot records under vaults and plans.

nano.notes: Same core; schedules run only while the tab is open.

differs: A backup is a Compute snapshot record of each disk (metadata only), so a restore creates empty disks of the same size.
Missed rule fires coalesce into one backup; the first sighting of a rule records a baseline only.
Long-running operations complete inline.

Organization and folder parents aggregate the single simulated project.
No attack paths, toxic combinations, BigQuery exports or resource value configs.

vertex-ai.title: Vertex AI
vertex-ai.summary: Vyomi's own Vertex AI control plane stores resources, while Gemini and embedding calls are answered by one small local model (llama.cpp on the appliance or booster, WebLLM on Nano).
wire: Vertex AI REST API v1/v1beta1 aiplatform.googleapis.com (endpoints, models, datasets, jobs, indexes, featureGroups, reasoningEngines, metadata)

offline.notes: core/gcp_vertex_core.py is the control plane; inference goes through the local-LLM seam (core/ai_models_core.py). With no model running the API returns 503 UNAVAILABLE rather than a canned answer; embeddings fall back to a deterministic hash embedding (vyomi-hash-embed).

nano.notes: Same control plane; inference only when the page registers a WebLLM model, otherwise 503. No GPU access beyond what the browser's WebGPU gives.

differs: One small model answers every Gemini model id, so quality is toy-grade; text, function calling and JSON responseSchema work, while images, audio, video, grounding, code execution, safety settings and tuning are rejected.
Embeddings from the hash fallback are stable and cosine-comparable but not semantic.
Only Gemini and text-embedding models are callable; deployed custom models answer :predict with 501 and no container serves them.
Training pipelines and custom jobs advance PENDING to SUCCEEDED on a roughly 5 s clock and never run containers.
Models, datasets, feature store and experiments are records only; model evaluation, copy and export are not simulated.
Workbench and Colab Enterprise are records: no JupyterLab server or VM starts.
Vector Search is exact brute-force nearest neighbour; no ANN tuning, restricts or sparse embeddings.
notInScope: Google-hosted Gemini models and real model quality
GPUs/TPUs for training and serving
Billing, quotas and Model Garden deployments

agent-engine.title: Agent Engine (Dev Simplified)
agent-engine.summary: reasoningEngines control plane is real, and :query / :streamQuery run a Vyomi agent spec as a tool-calling loop over the local model.
wire: typed google-cloud-aiplatform gapic clients with transport=rest

offline.notes: core/gcp_agentengine_core.py; agent spec in spec.vyomiAgentSpec or env VYOMI_AGENT_SPEC with declarative tools (static, template, calculator, webhook, in-process function).

nano.notes: Same loop; the loop re-runs after each model await so tools should be idempotent; webhook tools need egress, unavailable in the browser.

differs: Not a pickled Python class: vertexai.agent_engines.create(<object>), packageSpec/containerSpec, Memory Bank, Example Store and ADK/LangChain/LangGraph runtimes are not supported.
An engine with no spec answers FAILED_PRECONDITION; no model returns 503.
notInScope: Google-managed agent runtime
